question_text: A 62-year-old woman with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and rheumatoid arthritis presents for evaluation of elevated serum liver chemistries. She has had three months of intense, unremitting itching. Current medications include chlorthalidone, atorvastatin, and ibuprofen. Physical exam is unremarkable. Laboratory studies show aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 42 units/L, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 39 units/L, alkaline phosphatase 790 units/L, total bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL, and antimitochondrial antibody titer 1:80. What do you expect to see on liver biopsy?
